newsitem.title: USA: Dole barely ahead of Clinton in Texas - poll.
newsitem.headline: Dole barely ahead of Clinton in Texas - poll.

text.p: Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole was slightly ahead of President Bill Clinton among Texas voters in a poll conducted as the president was ordering missile attacks against Iraq last week, the Houston Chronicle reported on Sunday.
Dole was favoured by 44 percent of the 1,007 registered voters polled, compared with 41 percent for Clinton and 4 percent for Reform Party candidate Ross Perot, the newspaper reported.
"The giant sucking sound you hear is Ross Perot leaving the political arena in Texas," pollster Julie Weprin of Blum & Weprin Associates of New York told the Chronicle, using one of Perot's phrases.
The poll was conducted by Blum & Weprin September 2-5 and had a 3.5 percentage point margin of error.

In the poll, Clinton's approval rating as president jumped 12 percentage points since on January, with 52 percent of Texans voicing approval of the job he has done as president. Dole had a 58 percent approval rating among the Texas voters, while 63 percent had an unfavourable opinion of Perot, the poll said.
About one in three Texas voters said government spending and taxes was the most critical issue facing the country, and one in five considered education the most important issue, the poll said.
